analysis.title: GS US TMT .. today .. (Peter Callahan, 10 Nov 2026)
key_insights: NDX futures were down about 100 bps (SPX futures -60 bps) after the NDX's second best day in 18 months (+3.4% the prior day). The NDX closed just short of its cash 200-day moving average (27,995).

Investor conversations show nervous energy about a sustained rally into year-end. Investors are weighing hard questions on how linear data center (DC) builds will be in out-years against recent positives: strong 3Q earnings, financing visibility, relief in oil and rates, lowered expectations and a positioning reset.
The NDX trades at 18x-19x forward P/E and is up about 10% on the year.

Core CPI for October came in at +0.3% m/m. The note says the reading solidified market expectations for at least a +25 bps hike at the Dec 9 FOMC meeting (per WIRP, Bloomberg's rate-probability screen).

Top investor questions: memory stocks, durability of cloud service provider and Big Tech outperformance, earnings set-ups (CSCO, AMAT, NVDA), the internet view (gig names, OTAs), SE (-2%, was -7% at one point), the round-trip in TTD, and the lack of a bounce in DDOG after its print.
NVDA underperformed the semiconductor index (SOX) by nearly 11% the prior day, which the note calls the largest one-day underperformance this decade.

TTWO was +3% pre-market. The note says there is debate on how to trade the name near term (add before or after the launch) and how to manage expectations against the multi-year GTA 6 execution story. GIR (Sheridan) rates it BUY.

TTWO bull case: stock too cheap going into the GTA 6 cycle, beat/raise potential with multi-year growth visibility, and a self-help angle in Mobile (advertising improving sequentially, D2C channel growing).

TTWO bear case: F2Q net bookings and recurring consumer spending (RCS) were light because of NBA 2K27, nuances around the initial GTA launch and discovery value, volatility in Mobile (Color Block Jam), and uncertainty around AI tooling.

GS Econ's 2027 Consumer Outlook estimates consumer spending rose 2.5% in 2026 (Q4/Q4), driven by strong Q2 and Q3 as tax refunds and equity gains offset higher energy prices. It expects 2.2% growth in 2027 (Q4/Q4), with a softer start as higher rates weigh on durables, energy prices stay elevated and nonprofit spending falls after the midterms, then a pickup.

IFX was up about 2% in Europe after guiding FY27 revenue above consensus (about €20bn, implying +22% y/y) on AI power semiconductor demand. DC power semis revenue is expected to reach €4bn in FY27, broadly in line with investor expectations, and the automotive (ATV) segment is expected to grow mid-teens % in FY27.
The note observes that IFX trades closer to its decade-long range (€25-€45) than to the highs of the AI cycle, and asks why.

HRB is up nearly 100% from its lows and near a 52-week high. It reiterated F2027 guidance, so the near-term earnings outlook is unchanged. GIR (George) rates it SELL, saying consultative client experience and Second Look are unlikely to offset assisted share pressure in a low-growth industry, pointing to valuation downside risk.

Today's events: NFIB Small Business Index (97.8, flat m/m), US core CPI at 8:30am (est +0.3% m/m), earnings from BV, CRWV, FLY, RGTI, SONO and STUB, TSM October sales (+59.7% y/y), and investor days at FLEX, FDS and LYV.

market_movers.rationale: GIR (Sheridan) keeps its Buy. The bull case rests on multiple years of elevated EPS growth from the GTA 6 launch, and the bear case on light F2Q net bookings and RCS because of NBA 2K27.
GIR (George) keeps its Sell. Efforts to broaden the value proposition are unlikely to offset assisted share pressure in a low-growth industry, which points to valuation downside risk.
The stock underperformed the SOX by nearly 11% the prior day, the largest underperformance this decade. NVDA is also named among the earnings set-ups investors are asking about.
The stock rose 15% the prior day and another 20% after hours, then traded down 6% pre-market, a round-trip that investors are asking about.
FY27 guidance of about €20bn (+22% y/y) is above consensus, with DC power semis at about €4bn. The shares are still nearer the decade-long €25-€45 range than the AI-cycle highs.

earnings_insights: IFX (Infineon) guided FY27 revenue to about €20bn, implying +22% y/y, above consensus. DC power semis revenue is expected to reach €4bn in FY27, broadly in line with investor expectations, and ATV segment revenue is expected to grow mid-teens % (guidance, per GIR first take).
TTWO F2Q net bookings and RCS were light in the quarter because of NBA 2K27 (reported, per the bear case). The stock was +3% pre-market on 11/10.
HRB reiterated F2027 guidance on its F1Q report, a seasonally small quarter, leaving the near-term earnings outlook largely unchanged.
TSM October monthly sales were +59.7% y/y (scheduled for release 11/10).
Earnings due 11/10 after the close: BV, CRWV, FLY, RGTI, SONO, STUB. Investors are also asking about the CSCO, AMAT and NVDA set-ups.
DDOG has not bounced after its print, according to investor questions.
